title: 03 Data quality and drift detail (Tier 4 + Tier 0)

options.content:
Tier 0 (leading indicators, no labels needed) and Tier 4 (data quality and governance) share a board because they answer the same question from two sides: *has the input changed underneath a model we cannot yet evaluate?* Labels are 30-90 days out, so on any given day this board and `02 Serving SLO` are the only evidence that exists.

The drift panels are fed by the **monitoring workers**, not by the request path. PSI, KS and unseen-level rates all need the training baseline, and loading a reference distribution into the 150 ms decision budget is precisely what the import-linter contract exists to make impossible. The serving-side score distribution below is the half this process can honestly produce in real time, and it is the one that answers first: the workers run on a schedule measured in minutes.

Panels still marked **AWAITING** need a window over more than one event (duplicates, out-of-order, training-serving skew) or a governance artifact that is not a runtime observation (assumption freshness).

panels.title: Score distribution PSI vs training baseline
panels.description: LIVE, from the monitoring workers. The earliest possible warning. 0.25 is `monitoring.drift.PSI_ALERT_THRESHOLD` and the FraudLensScoreDrift page; 0.10-0.25 is the watch band that lives here and does not page.

panels.title: Serving score distribution by bucket (share of traffic)
panels.description: LIVE. The serving half of the PSI computation, and useful on its own: the bucket edges are concentrated where the decision boundaries actually sit (break-even runs 0.369 to 0.740 across amount and tenure), so a shift across a boundary is visible here rather than smeared across a 0.1-wide bin. Degraded decisions contribute nothing to this series - a fallback decision has no probability, and recording 0.0 would make the distribution look calm during an outage.

panels.title: Top-10 drifting features (PSI / KS)
panels.description: LIVE, from the monitoring workers, and today it carries one series - the score itself, which `monitoring.report` treats as a monitored feature. It widens to per-column PSI as E7 extends the baseline to the feature vector; `topk` is here from the start because 225 series on one panel is a picture, not a diagnosis.

panels.title: Null rate and unseen categorical level rate
panels.description: Null rate is the leading cause of silent failure: a feature that starts arriving empty does not raise, it just prices every customer as an average one. Unseen-level rate is entity churn - new cards, new devices, new email domains - which is normal at a low rate and a pipeline break at a high one. Both come from the monitoring workers, which hold the training baseline - the request path deliberately does not, because loading a reference distribution into the 150 ms budget is what the import-linter contract forbids. Read against the trailing window rather than against the baseline null rate, which lives inside the baseline artifact and is not exported as a series; that is a stated gap, not an approximation to ignore.

panels.title: Missing tenure signal (priced as median)
panels.description: LIVE, and the alerting one - see FraudLensDataBreakage. `days_since_first_seen` is the only input whose absence changes the *price*: without it the relationship-cost term falls back to the median, which moves the false-positive arm and therefore the whole decision boundary. Surfaced as a reason code on the decision itself, so a disputing customer can be told the assumption was applied to them.

panels.title: Reason-code mix
panels.description: LIVE. Note what this is NOT: `reason-code coverage` from the Tier 4 catalog is not plotted, because the response contract enforces at least one code (`min_length=1`, asserted by contract test) and a coverage gauge would read 100% forever - a metric that cannot move is worse than no metric, since it reads as evidence. The mix is the signal instead. A surge in a FALLBACK_RULE_* code is an outage; a surge in UNKNOWN_TENURE_PRICED_AS_MEDIAN is an upstream break; a shift between SCORE_ABOVE_* codes is the policy binding somewhere new.

panels.title: Schema violation rate (422) and unpersisted decisions
panels.description: LIVE, both halves. 422 IS the schema-violation rate: the request contract runs strict validation with extra="forbid", so a 422 means a caller sent a field, a type or a naive timestamp it did not send yesterday - and a malformed request produced no decision and wrote nothing, which is why it must never be counted as a degraded decision. Unpersisted decisions are the serving-side view of Tier 4 'complete lineage': the customer got a correct decision that we cannot reconstruct, which is an auditability incident rather than an error. It was previously only a log line.

panels.title: Training-serving skew, duplicates, out-of-order events - AWAITING E7
panels.description: All three need to see two of something and a single request sees one. Skew compares the offline and online score for the same row and has a zero threshold - it invalidates every offline number we hold. Duplicate and out-of-order rates are ledger-side. NOTE on out-of-order: a naive 'event time vs wall clock' lag metric is deliberately NOT emitted from the request path, because this deployment replays a 182-day historical window - event time is months behind wall clock by design, so that metric would either page constantly or be tuned until it means nothing.

panels.title: Assumption freshness: days since P(churn|declined) reviewed - AWAITING E7/E9
panels.description: BUSINESS ASSUMPTION TRACKER. P(churn|declined) has no data support in IEEE-CIS - it is tenure-graded from published false-decline research - and it drives the entire false-positive cost term, and therefore every decline boundary in the system. Production tooling cannot fix an unmeasurable input, so it is treated the way a risk organisation treats a number it cannot measure: a versioned artifact with a named owner, a review date, a sensitivity analysis, and this staleness counter. Making the softest number the most visible one is the point. The `owner` label is on the series so the panel names who is overdue.

panels.title: Decision value by amount band ($/hour through each arm)
panels.description: LIVE. Tier 1's 'decline $ / approve $ by amount band' - where the policy binds. Bands come from the amount histogram's buckets rather than from a metric label, because the band boundaries are a business constant owned by `serving.reasons` and a second copy in a label would be a second definition of it. The bucket edges sit at the published break-even inflection points: under $25 we must be 73% sure to decline, at $500+ only 37%, which inverts the intuition most fraud teams operate on.

panels.title: Monitoring job health - is the thing that watches still watching?
panels.description: LIVE. Every Tier 0 and Tier 2 panel in this system is produced by a scheduled worker, which means a worker that has silently stopped leaves boards that look calm because nothing is updating them. This is the panel that distinguishes 'quiet' from 'dead'. `tier2_refusals` is not an error rate: refusing an immature window is the correct behaviour (spec 4.2 refuses rather than warns), and a sustained refusal count is the honest statement that we cannot yet evaluate the model. `baseline_info` carries the baseline_id every drift number on this board is measured against - if it changes, the comparison changed and the history above is not continuous.

panels.title: Serving counters vs ledger-derived rates (reconciliation)
panels.description: LIVE, and deliberately redundant. The same two quantities are measured twice by independent paths: the request path increments a counter as it decides, and the monitoring job recomputes the rates from the decision ledger. They should agree. When they do not, the gap IS the measurement - it means decisions were served but not persisted, which is an auditability incident that no error-rate panel would show because those requests returned 200. Read alongside `unpersisted decisions/min`.
